sentences.text: Lonchidion is an extinct genus of shark belonging to the class Chondrichthyes and the family Lonchidiidae.
A preserved specimen of Lonchidion is among the smallest known elasmobranchs, measuring around 3.5 cm in length.
The animal possessed low-crowned teeth likely adapted for grinding hard prey through durophagy.
Richard Estes first described the genus Lonchidion in 1964, establishing L. selachas as the type species.
Fossils are frequently found in freshwater and brackish deposits, suggesting Lonchidion was thought to be euryhaline.
Fossils of Lonchidion have been discovered worldwide.
The time range for Lonchidion spans from the Carnian to the Maastrichtian, approximately 237 to 66 million years ago, extending from the Middle Triassic to the very end of the Cretaceous.
Some authors debate the validity of Lonchidion as a genus, suggesting its teeth represent a juvenile morphological type lost in adults rather than a distinct genus.
